original_question.question: A square piece of paper is folded in half by moving its left half onto its right half, then folded in half by moving its bottom half onto its top half. The resulting four-layer square is shown, with A at the intersection of the two folded edges and B, C, D in counterclockwise order. Make two straight cuts parallel to AD, meeting AB at one-quarter and three-quarters of the way from A to B, each continuing to DC. Make a third straight cut parallel to AB, meeting AD one-quarter of the way from A to D and continuing to BC. The dashed segments in the figure are cuts, not fold lines; cut through every layer only along those segments. Unfold every resulting piece as far as possible. How many resulting pieces are squares? Pieces are counted separately; a shape with a hole is not a square.
